abstract: Amid rising concerns over the emissions of greenhouse gases and climate change, the imperative to reduce corporate carbon emissions has become increasingly critical. This study constructs a novel theoretical model for exploring the collaborative governance and anti-competitive views on the role of common institutional investors (CIIs) in corporate carbon emissions. Using a sample of Chinese A-share-listed manufacturing firms from 2009 to 2021, our results show strong evidence of the anti-competitive view, suggesting that CIIs play a collusive role in affecting corporate carbon emissions positively. Greater market power of CIIs and intensified industry competition are found to be the underlying mechanisms. Notably, the anti-competitive effect of CIIs is more pronounced in firms with market-driven short-term CIIs, low financing constraints, and those in low-carbon industries. Additionally, our further evidence shows that industry competition amplifies the anti-competitive effect of CIIs by strengthening their incentives to reduce costly environmental competition among portfolio firms. By shedding light on the relationship between CIIs and corporate carbon emissions, the study provides valuable insights into whether there should be incentives or restrictions on CIIs in achieving carbon reduction and addressing global challenges in sustainable development.

title: Being collaborative or collusive? The role of common institutional investors in corporate carbon emissions

abstract: Many U.S. states have adopted the goal of achieving carbon neutrality in the coming decades. Pathways for achieving these targets would likely yield a reduction of air pollutant emissions as well. We assess several state-level decarbonization pathways for Massachusetts, including electrification of buildings and transportation and decarbonization of the electric grid, estimating their impacts on in- and out-of-state emissions of carbon dioxide (CO2) and several air pollutants. The analysis applies the GCAM-USA integrated assessment model with state-level resolution. We consider interactions between existing and proposed state and regional policies. The most aggressive state decarbonization pathway that was examined would achieve only a 65% reduction in CO2 emissions by 2050 relative to 2015, indicating the need for further decarbonization options within the industry and non-road transportation sectors to achieve net-zero emission goal stated by the current administration. The air pollution co-benefits under these decarbonization pathways are substantial, especially for primary fine particulate matter. While policies focusing only on Massachusetts are shown to deliver in-state reductions of CO2 and air pollutant emissions, these reductions were partially countered by emissions increases in other states, indicating the need for coordinated regional planning to prevent emissions leakage.
title: Future in- and out-of-state air pollutant emissions under decarbonization pathways for Massachusetts

abstract: Standard growth accounting exercises with intermediate goods often hold the intermediate input share of gross output fixed. This study shows that this assumption can materially change measured productivity when production structures evolve. We develop a national accounts–consistent framework in which sectoral intermediate input intensities vary over time, and apply it to agriculture, manufacturing, and services in 14 advanced economies spanning 1995–2020. The mechanism is simple—if gross output and intermediate expenditures are observed but the intermediate share is forced to remain constant, measured value-added must absorb the inconsistency and the total factor productivity (TFP) residual changes. The resulting gaps are quantitatively meaningful. By 2020, aggregate TFP under the constant-share approach was about 26% higher in Luxembourg and 13% higher in Germany, but about 8% lower in Latvia. Therefore, productivity measurement in multisector models should account for changing production structures, particularly as supply chains and input–output linkages evolve.
title: Growth accounting with time-varying input intensities

abstract: We study how accounting standards shape macroeconomic outcomes. While prior research typically assumes perfectly elastic capital supply, we model it as upward-sloping, so investors’ rate of return (entrepreneurs’ cost of capital) is determined by supply and demand. Because accounting standards govern the reports used in funding decisions, they shift capital demand, changing the equilibrium rate and redistributing surplus between entrepreneurs and investors. Conservative standards shrink the pool of firms seeking capital, lowering the cost of capital for funded entrepreneurs. Conservatism can therefore benefit entrepreneurs as a group, yet no entrepreneur would adopt it individually because each takes the market rate as given. Liberal standards can benefit investors by raising the rate despite reducing investment efficiency. Our findings imply that the FASB’s focus on providing decision-useful information can paradoxically harm investors by reducing capital demand. These distributional conflicts explain why unbiased standards may face resistance despite maximizing total welfare.
title: Macroeconomic implications of accounting standards

abstract: This article revisits the claim that Holland owed much of its seventeenth‐century efflorescence to the absence of feudal constraints on its economy. Because Holland was relatively late to develop in the eleventh and twelfth centuries, it supposedly missed the European Feudal Revolution, thus opening space for an exceptional long‐run development. Whilst this view is correct for serfdom and landlordship, it is not for seigneurial lordship, another constituent of feudalism as a controversial concept. A survey reveals that seigneuries were not rarer than in other Netherlandish principalities. Seigneurial surplus‐extraction, which might have stifled economic innovation, was low, but this too was not unique to Holland. Rather than being a stumbling block for dynamism, however, seigneuries supported economic change. Apart from shielding burgeoning rural proto‐industries from urban rent‐seeking, seigneurial regulations put in place a framework for the rise of factor markets for land and labour. There is truth to the claim that the Holland countryside was an open society that prospered thanks to secure property rights and the agency for villagers to pursue a wide range of strategies, but Holland did not have these advantages because it was free of lordship. In fact, seigneuries were part of its exceptional political economy.
title: Seigneurial institutions and Holland's seventeenth‐century miracle

abstract: This paper explores the relationship between different notions of local incentive compatibility (LIC) and incentive compatibility (IC) within ordinally restricted type-spaces. We introduce the concepts of ordinal local–global equivalence (OLGE) and cardinal local–global equivalence (CLGE) environments, establishing their equivalence in the context of strict ordinally restricted type-spaces. We then extend our analysis to type-spaces that admit indifference, where we define almost everywhere IC and strong LIC, and provide the necessary and sufficient condition for their equivalence. Additionally, we present a framework for minimally checking the IC property of a mechanism in any ordinally restricted type-space, showing that the set of incentive constraints between local types and boundary types together form a minimal set of incentive constraints ensuring (full) incentive compatibility.
title: Local incentive compatibility in ordinally restricted type-spaces

abstract: We study a generalization of the standard queueing problem which introduces a deadline of each agent. For the queueing problem with deadlines, or simple the deadline queueing problem, each agent should be served before her deadline. We propose two rules for the problem, called the deadline-adjusted minimal and the deadline-adjusted maximal transfer rules, which are natural modifications of two of the most well-known rules for the standard queueing problem, the minimal and the maximal transfer rules, respectively, and present their axiomatic characterizations. The deadline-adjusted minimal transfer rule is the only rule jointly satisfying constrained efficiency, Pareto indifference, equal treatment of equals, positional invariance, full compensation, and independence of preceding larger costs. On the other hand, the deadline-adjusted maximal transfer rule is the only rule jointly satisfying constrained efficiency, Pareto indifference, equal treatment of equals, positional invariance, full compensation, and independence of following smaller costs.
title: Queueing with deadlines: Characterizing two transfer rules

abstract: We study whether bank loan portfolios help explain differences in their stock returns during major disruptions to foreign trade. Using stock market reactions during the 2018 U.S.-China trade war and the April 2025 tariff announcements, we identify industries that are systematically vulnerable and resilient to trade disruptions. We then combine these classifications with confidential supervisory lending data to construct a measure of trade exposure for large U.S. banks. We find that banks with greater exposure experienced significantly larger stock price declines following the April 2025 tariff announcements.

abstract: We examine lithium and development imaginaries in mining-dependent Peru, asking: What are these imaginaries? What narratives underpin them? Who articulates and shares them, and from where? What forms of state (in)action are envisioned in relation to them? The case study elucidates how alternative “imagined futures” coexist within a natural resource–dependent economy. The ruling national elites in Lima have a neoliberal imagination, treating lithium like any other mineral resource in the country. In contrast, professional elites in the mineral-rich but peripheral region of Puno adopt a resource nationalist view, advocating for direct state involvement in lithium industrialization and the transformation of the domestic energy system, shaped by beliefs on Bolivia’s developmental pathway. Among rural community leaders as well as political and social leaders in the districts near lithium and uranium deposits, however, the prevailing idea is that of a social license. In this view, each community has the capacity to negotiate development terms with mining companies independently. In the broader imagination at the resource periphery of a peripheral national economy, the state is perceived primarily as a minimalist governmental actor, necessary only to oversee and ensure the enforcement of mine-community agreements and to provide basic infrastructure. Thus, elites at the political center and communities near expected resource developments converge in their immediate pursuit of rents promised by resource commodification. In the dominant discourses, environmental concerns are often subordinated to economic development goals.
title: Dependent development at the energy transition: placing lithium imaginaries in Neoliberal and Contentious Peru

abstract: We document that the convenience yield of U.S. Treasuries exhibits properties consistent with a hedging perspective of safe assets, that is, Treasuries are valued highly if they appreciate with poor aggregate shocks. In particular, the convenience yield tends to be low when the covariance of Treasury returns with the aggregate stock market returns is high. A decomposition of the aggregate stock‐bond covariance into terms corresponding to the convenience yield, the frictionless risk‐free rate, and default risk reveals that the covariance between stock returns and the convenience yield itself drives the effect in a substantive capacity.
title: When Do Treasuries Earn the Convenience Yield?—A Hedging Perspective

abstract: The rapid expansion of ridesharing services like Uber and Lyft has transformed urban transportation, yet their effects on crime remain underexplored. Leveraging a natural experiment from their staggered rollout across U.S. cities, this study examines how ridesharing influences crime rates. Using a two‐way fixed effects model, I find that ridesharing services reduce violent crimes by 4.6%, property crimes by 5.6%, and burglaries by 10.5%, while the baseline estimates show no significant effects on larceny, motor vehicle theft, or arson. Exploring potential mechanisms, I show that improved employment opportunities generated by ridesharing platforms play a key role in these crime reductions.
abstract_zh: 优步和来福车等网约车服务的迅速扩张改变了城市交通，但其对犯罪的影响仍未得到充分探讨。本研究利用这些服务在美国各城市交错推出的自然实验，考察网约车如何影响犯罪率。使用双向固定效应模型，我发现网约车服务使暴力犯罪减少4.6%，财产犯罪减少5.6%，入室盗窃减少10.5%，而基准估计显示对盗窃、机动车盗窃或纵火没有显著影响。在探讨潜在机制时，我表明网约车平台带来的就业机会改善在这些犯罪减少中发挥了关键作用。
title: Crime on the move? The effect of ridesharing services on crime
title_zh: 移动中的犯罪？网约车服务对犯罪的影响

abstract: We exploit variation in access to Mexico's early-1900s railroad network to estimate its short- and long-run effects on US migration. Instrumenting access with least-cost paths between historical cities, we find that railroads increased migration rates fourfold, while also spurring urbanization and development. The key mechanism was sequential migration: railroads channeled people to railroad hubs, then onward to the US. A century later, long after railroads became obsolete, railroad-connected locations show lower migration rates, consistent with growth reducing emigration incentives. Yet destination choices persist: locations that favored specific US destinations in the 1900s still do today, reflecting durable migrant networks.
abstract_zh: 我们利用墨西哥20世纪初铁路网络可达性的差异，估计其对美国移民的短期和长期影响。以历史城市之间的最低成本路径作为可达性的工具变量，我们发现铁路使移民率提高了四倍，同时也推动了城市化和经济发展。关键机制是链式移民：铁路将人们引导至铁路枢纽，再由此前往美国。一个世纪之后，在铁路早已被淘汰很久之后，与铁路相连的地点显示出更低的移民率，这与经济增长降低移民激励相一致。然而，目的地选择却持续存在：20世纪初倾向于特定美国目的地的地方，今天依然如此，反映出移民网络的持久性。
china_relevance_reason: 研究对象为墨西哥铁路网络与墨西哥-美国移民，数据与制度背景均为墨西哥，不涉及中国。
title: The Short- and Long-Run Effects of Railroads on Mexico-US Migration
title_zh: 铁路对墨西哥-美国移民的短期和长期影响

abstract: This paper examines the territorial reconfiguration of American electoral politics since the 1980s, tracing the remaking of Republican support from Reagan’s 1984 landslide to Trump’s three presidential campaigns (2016, 2020, 2024). Drawing on panel data for every presidential election from 1984 to 2024 across 722 commuting zones, we test whether regional development traps, defined as enduring economic underperformance, explain both the shift from Democrats to Republicans and the Republicans’ internal realignment. Mundlak/Correlated Random Effects estimates show backlash is overwhelmingly driven by structural, not cyclical, decline. Short-term economic fluctuations do not predict Republican swing, while long-run territorial position does so decisively. Voters are not responding to recessions. They are registering alienation from an economic order that has failed their communities for a generation. Trump’s gains concentrated in places persistently left behind, whose peripheral position has become entrenched.
abstract_zh: 本文考察了20世纪80年代以来美国选举政治的地域重构，追溯了共和党支持基础从1984年里根压倒性胜利到特朗普三次总统竞选（2016年、2020年、2024年）的重塑过程。基于1984年至2024年每一次总统选举中722个通勤区的面板数据，我们检验了区域发展陷阱——定义为持续的经济表现不佳——是否能够解释从民主党向共和党的转变以及共和党内部的重新结盟。Mundlak/相关随机效应估计表明，这种反弹绝大多数由结构性衰退而非周期性衰退驱动。短期经济波动不能预测共和党选情的变化，而长期地域位置则具有决定性的预测作用。选民并非在回应经济衰退。他们表达的是对一个辜负其社区长达一代人的经济秩序的疏离感。特朗普的 gains 集中在那些长期被遗弃的地方，这些地方的外围地位已经根深蒂固。
title: From Reagan to Trump: Regional development traps and the remaking of American electoral politics
title_zh: 从里根到特朗普：区域发展陷阱与美国选举政治的重塑

abstract: Whether earnings premia in licensed occupations reflect human capital or scarcity rents is hard to identify, because training and licensing are bundled. We exploit a reform at Uruguay's main university that shortened the accounting degree and granted a license, without additional learning requirements, to students already working alongside incumbent accountants. Competition from these new licensees identifies changes in licensing rents, separate from returns to training. Incumbent accountants' earnings fell by about 9 percent relative to comparable professionals, with no change in employment, consistent with licensing rents.
abstract_zh: 持证职业中的收入溢价反映的是人力资本还是稀缺租金，这一问题难以识别，因为培训与执照发放往往捆绑在一起。我们利用乌拉圭主要大学的一项改革：该改革缩短了会计学位的学习年限，并在没有额外学习要求的情况下，向已在在职会计师身边工作的学生授予执照。来自这些新持证者的竞争，使我们能够识别执照租金的变化，并将其与培训回报区分开来。在职会计师的收入相对于可比专业人士下降了约9%，而就业没有变化，这与执照租金的存在相一致。
title: Occupational Licensing Without Learning
title_zh: 无学习效应的职业许可

abstract: This paper examines how risk attitudes and social preferences shape support for redistributive and environmental policies. We propose a micro-founded explanation in which support for redistribution arises from two mechanisms: an insurance motive and fairness concerns. Both risk aversion and social preferences increase demand for redistribution, with a substitution effect whereby higher aversion to social risk lowers the threshold of social preferences needed to support it. For environmental protection, these factors operate in parallel, increasing support for policies that mitigate negative consumption externalities. When individuals choose between policy domains, preferences depend on perceived future income uncertainty and the weight assigned to externalities, making the overall effect ambiguous. We test these predictions using a nationally representative dataset of 6,000 observations from six European countries. The empirical results confirm our hypotheses.
abstract_zh: 本文考察风险态度与社会偏好如何影响对再分配政策和环境政策的支持。我们提出一个微观基础解释，其中对再分配的支持源于两种机制：保险动机与公平关切。风险厌恶和社会偏好都会增加对再分配的需求，并存在替代效应，即对社会风险的厌恶程度越高，支持再分配所需的社会偏好阈值就越低。对于环境保护，这些因素并行发挥作用，增加对缓解负消费外部性政策的支持。当个人在不同政策领域之间进行选择时，偏好取决于感知到的未来收入不确定性以及赋予外部性的权重，从而使总体效应变得不确定。我们使用来自六个欧洲国家、包含6000个观测值的全国代表性数据集检验这些预测。实证结果证实了我们的假设。
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
title: Risk and Social Preferences: Theory and Evidence on Support for Redistribution and Environmental Protection
title_zh: 风险与社会偏好：关于再分配和环境保护支持的理论与证据

abstract: This paper examines crowdfunding of a risky, constant-returns project. The crowdfunder chooses a threshold and interest rate. These jointly determine profit and welfare outcomes by influencing investors’ decisions to acquire information and to bid and by aggregating the information their bids reveal into a project funding decision. A higher threshold funds fewer projects but, fixing investor strategies, raises the ratio of good to bad quality among those that get funded by a factor we call the “crowdblessing.” At the same time, raising the threshold, or the interest rate, reduces incentives to acquire and use private information. Optimal design trades off crowdblessing against investment scale. Surprisingly, profit-maximizers sometimes induce excessive information acquisition to limit investor rent. In our comparative statics, information acquisition falls with the cost of information and with prior optimism but precision has an ambiguous impact. Costly information reduces welfare but may raise profits by facilitating rent-extraction.
abstract_zh: 本文考察了一个具有风险且规模报酬不变项目的众筹问题。众筹发起人选择门槛和利率。二者通过影响投资者获取信息以及出价的决定，并将投资者出价所揭示的信息汇总为项目融资决策，共同决定利润与福利结果。较高的门槛会减少获得融资的项目数量，但在固定投资者策略的情况下，会提高获得融资项目中优质项目与劣质项目的比例，其倍数我们称之为“众筹祝福”。与此同时，提高门槛或利率会削弱投资者获取和使用私人信息的激励。最优设计需要在众筹祝福与投资规模之间进行权衡。令人意外的是，利润最大化者有时会诱发过度信息获取，以限制投资者租金。在我们的比较静态分析中，信息获取随信息成本和先验乐观程度上升而下降，但精确度的影响并不明确。高成本信息会降低福利，但可能通过便利租金抽取而提高利润。
title: Optimal investment-based crowdfunding: crowdblessing versus scale
title_zh: 基于最优投资的众筹：众筹祝福与规模

abstract: Discussion of Fang, Huang, Wang, and Yang (2026).
title: Discussion of “Sex and the City: Demographics, Spatial Sorting, and the Marriage Market”
title_zh: 对《欲望都市：人口统计、空间分选与婚姻市场》的讨论

abstract: Formalizing Indigenous land rights is critical for environmental justice and sustainable development. Yet legal recognition often creates new territorial governing bodies tasked with managing collective lands, whose legitimacy cannot be assumed. This study examines how trust in Indigenous territorial authorities is built, contested, and withdrawn following the formalization of collective land rights in the Honduran Moskitia. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork and household interviews in three villages across diverse socio-ecological settings, the study analyzes how residents assess their territorial authorities. The analysis treats trust as multidimensional and relational. The study examines different forms of trust—dispositional, rational, affinitive, and procedural—to identify the rationales that drive assessments of authority in each village. These rationales are interpreted through the lens of a Miskitu moral economy, framing trust assessments in terms of what residents expect of a territorial authority to be considered legitimate. A moral economy lens contributes analytically to a multidimensional trust framework by explaining why certain forms of trust feel more salient when evaluating authority performance and how they interact with one another. The central finding is that the socio-spatial configuration of land conflicts shapes which evaluative dimensions of trust become most salient. A multidimensional and relational trust analysis contributes a more granular understanding of this process: it shows how different forms of trust interact and shift through everyday encounters with authority, identifying the specific points at which legitimacy is strengthened, strained, or quietly lost.
abstract_zh: 将原住民土地权利正式化对于环境正义与可持续发展至关重要。然而，法律承认往往催生出负责管理集体土地的新领土治理机构，而这些机构的合法性并不能被预设。本研究考察在洪都拉斯莫斯基蒂亚集体土地权利正式化之后，对原住民领土当局的信任如何被建立、争夺与撤回。研究依托在三个处于不同社会—生态环境的村庄中开展的民族志田野调查与家庭访谈，分析居民如何评价其领土当局。分析将信任视为多维且关系性的。研究考察不同形式的信任——倾向性信任、理性信任、亲缘性信任与程序性信任——以识别在每个村庄中驱动权威评价的依据。这些依据通过米斯基图道德经济的视角加以解读，将信任评价置于居民对领土当局被视为合法所抱持期待的框架之中。道德经济视角在分析上有助于多维信任框架，因为它解释了为何某些信任形式在评价权威绩效时显得更为突出，以及它们如何相互作用。核心发现是，土地冲突的社会—空间配置塑造了哪些信任评价维度最为突出。多维且关系性的信任分析有助于更细致地理解这一过程：它展示了不同形式的信任如何在与权威的日常遭遇中相互作用并发生转变，并识别出合法性被强化、被拉紧或悄然丧失的具体节点。
title: Governing Indigenous territories: trust, moral economy, and the legitimation of Indigenous territorial authority in the Honduran Moskitia
title_zh: 治理原住民领地：洪都拉斯莫斯基蒂亚地区的信任、道德经济与原住民领地权威的合法化

abstract: I show how firms optimize the allocation of charitable funds around investments that require external stakeholder support, such as mergers and acquisitions. Acquirers increase donations to target‐related charities before making a takeover offer, but scale funds back after withdrawing from a deal. Firms redistribute funds from nontakeover‐related areas to target insider–affiliated charities, employee communities, and counties with a regulatory presence. Targeted donations that encourage blockholder reciprocity and employee commitment are associated with better deal performance through decreased merger premiums and lower integration costs. Overall, the results highlight firms’ use of philanthropy to manage stakeholder relations in takeover decisions.
abstract_zh: 我展示了企业如何在需要外部利益相关者支持的投資（如并购）周围优化慈善资金配置。收购方在提出收购要约前会增加对目标相关慈善机构的捐赠，但在退出交易后则会缩减资金。企业将资金从与收购无关的领域重新分配到目标内部人关联的慈善机构、员工社区以及设有监管机构的县。旨在鼓励大股东互惠和员工承诺的定向捐赠，通过降低并购溢价和整合成本，与更好的交易表现相关联。总体而言，这些结果凸显了企业在收购决策中利用慈善事业来管理利益相关者关系。
title: Targeted Philanthropy: Evidence from M&As
title_zh: 定向慈善：来自并购的证据

abstract: We examine how behavioral incentives affect goal setting and performance when individuals choose their own goals. Using a model with reference-dependent preferences and effort cost uncertainty, we predict that commitment mechanisms improve performance by inducing more conservative goal selection to increase goal attainability, whereas prosocial incentives enhance performance by increasing motivation. Two experiments confirm these predictions. In an online real-effort task, soft commitment reduced goals relative to controls but significantly increased performance, whereas prosocial incentives, in the form of charitable donations contingent on goal achievement, preserved goal ambition and improved performance without lowering goals. A four-week field experiment in which students set daily exercise goals yields similar results: commitment lowered goals while increasing performance, whereas prosocial incentives maintained ambitious goals and improved outcomes. These effects persisted throughout the experiment. These findings highlight that, under effort cost uncertainty, commitment and prosocial incentives improve performance through distinct mechanisms.
abstract_zh: 我们考察当个体自行选择目标时，行为激励如何影响目标设定与绩效。利用一个具有参照依赖偏好和努力成本不确定性的模型，我们预测：承诺机制通过诱导更保守的目标选择以提高目标可实现性来改善绩效，而亲社会激励则通过增强动机来提升绩效。两项实验证实了这些预测。在一项在线真实努力任务中，相较于控制组，软承诺降低了目标，但显著提高了绩效；而以与目标达成挂钩的慈善捐赠形式提供的亲社会激励，则保持了目标雄心，并在不降低目标的情况下改善了绩效。一项为期四周、让学生设定每日锻炼目标的实地实验得到了类似结果：承诺降低了目标，同时提高了绩效；而亲社会激励则维持了雄心勃勃的目标并改善了结果。这些效应在整个实验期间持续存在。这些发现凸显出，在努力成本不确定性下，承诺与亲社会激励通过不同机制改善绩效。
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
title: Aim high or play safe? Commitment, prosocial incentives, and goal setting
title_zh: 志存高远还是稳中求进？承诺、亲社会激励与目标设定

abstract: The definition and quantification of fuel (or energy) poverty remain contentious, particularly within the English policy landscape. The current official definition—Low Income Low Energy Efficiency (LILEE)—systematically underestimates the condition in low- and middle-income households, effectively obfuscating changing energy affordability norms. This paper presents a sensitivity analysis of fuel poverty trajectories in Nottingham, UK, across competing definitions and diverging ‘optimistic’ (domestic efficiency upgrades) and ‘pessimistic’ (energy price inflation) scenarios. Results demonstrate that LILEE overstates the efficacy of efficiency upgrades while failing to adequately reflect the impact of price shocks. To address these deficiencies, we propose the Temporal Equity Framework (TEF), a budget standard-based approach paired with a proportional energy expenditure indicator that captures shifting affordability norms more equitably. The TEF also introduces continuous expenditure-based depth indicators to evaluate the entrenchment of fuel-poor households (the ‘fuel poverty gap’) and the resilience of non-fuel-poor households (the ‘fuel poverty buffer’). We argue that responsive definitions which also recognise fuel poverty as a continuum of vulnerability, rather than a static, dichotomous state, are paramount to ensuring the equitability of energy transitions. Further, we suggest that the early identification of fuel poverty and spatial targeting of remedial resources could be markedly improved by adopting the TEF. We conclude that the adoption of a multidimensional budget standard-based definition is essential to facilitate a more accurate and just evaluation of energy transitions in England.
abstract_zh: 燃料（或能源）贫困的定义与量化仍存在争议，尤其在英格兰政策语境中更是如此。当前官方定义——低收入低能效（LILEE）——系统性地低估了中低收入家庭的燃料贫困状况，实际上掩盖了不断变化的能源可负担性规范。本文对英国诺丁汉的燃料贫困轨迹进行了敏感性分析，比较了相互竞争的定义以及分化的“乐观”（家庭能效升级）与“悲观”（能源价格上涨）情景。结果表明，LILEE高估了能效升级的效果，同时未能充分反映价格冲击的影响。为弥补这些缺陷，我们提出时间公平框架（TEF），这是一种基于预算标准的方法，并搭配比例能源支出指标，从而更公平地捕捉不断变化的可负担性规范。TEF还引入了基于连续支出的深度指标，以评估燃料贫困家庭的固化程度（“燃料贫困缺口”）和非燃料贫困家庭的韧性（“燃料贫困缓冲”）。我们认为，具有响应性的定义——同时将燃料贫困视为一种脆弱性的连续谱，而非静态的二分状态——对于确保能源转型的公平性至关重要。此外，我们建议，采用TEF可显著改进燃料贫困的早期识别和补救资源的空间靶向配置。我们得出结论：采用基于预算标准的多维定义，对于促进英格兰能源转型更准确、更公正的评估至关重要。
title: Redefining fuel poverty: Introducing the temporal equity framework (TEF)
title_zh: 重新定义燃料贫困：引入时间公平框架（TEF）

abstract: Geopolitical tensions are often seen as a source of inflation. But this is only part of the story. This column shows that geopolitical shocks transmitted through energy markets raise prices while depressing economic activity. But geopolitical shocks unrelated to energy markets reduce inflation instead. These two shocks can be identified based on oil prices and geopolitical risk dynamics around major geopolitical events.
abstract_zh: 地缘政治紧张局势常被视为通胀的来源。但这只是故事的一部分。本专栏表明，通过能源市场传导的地缘政治冲击会推高价格，同时抑制经济活动。但与能源市场无关的地缘政治冲击反而会降低通胀。基于重大地缘政治事件前后的油价和地缘政治风险动态，可以识别出这两类冲击。
title: Not all geopolitical shocks are inflationary
title_zh: 并非所有地缘政治冲击都会引发通胀

abstract: Rising income inequality in Western high-income countries threatens democratic governance and social cohesion, and AI risks making it worse. Drawing on a forthcoming book, this column argues for worker-managed firms as a durable remedy. With no external owners taking profits, worker cooperatives protect against the rising bargaining power of employers and provide an enhanced sense of self-worth and self-determination for employees. Furthermore, the data suggest that well-designed worker cooperatives compete with conventional firms in free markets with no evidence of a productivity gap. Because they are underprovided by the market, it calls for government action to support worker cooperatives.
abstract_zh: 西方高收入国家收入不平等的加剧威胁着民主治理和社会凝聚力，而人工智能可能使其进一步恶化。基于一本即将出版的著作，本专栏主张将劳动者管理的企业作为一种持久补救方案。由于不存在外部所有者攫取利润，劳动者合作社能够抵御雇主议价能力的上升，并为员工提供更强的自我价值感和自主感。此外，数据表明，设计良好的劳动者合作社能够在自由市场中与传统企业竞争，且没有证据显示存在生产率差距。由于市场对劳动者合作社的供给不足，因此需要政府采取行动予以支持。
title: Worker-managed firms can curb inequality and protect free markets
title_zh: 工人管理的企业可以抑制不平等并保护自由市场

abstract: Average actual hours worked (AAHW) have declined across many advanced economies, affecting aggregate labor input and potential output. This paper examines the evolution of AAHW in Nordic countries between 2011 and 2022, with a focus on educational attainment and complementary ++gender, employment status, and citizenship. Using microdata from the European Union Labour Force Survey and a Shapley decomposition, the analysis shows that the decline in AAHW is primarily driven by reductions in hours among workers with lower and medium levels of educational attainment, used here as a proxy for skill levels. By contrast, highly educated workers work longer hours and their increasing share partly offsets the decline. Our decompositions show that this education-based result remains robust when worker groups are further split by age, gender and full-time/part-time status, and that most of the citizenship-related variation is concentrated among citizens, with non-citizen contributions generally smaller and often offsetting. Finland represents a temporary pandemic and post-pandemic exception, although the overall contribution of tertiary-educated workers remains positive. Supplementary evidence comparing desired and usual hours shows larger positive gaps among less-educated workers, while tertiary-educated workers in several countries appear closer to, or at times above, their preferred hours. These patterns are consistent with constraints on realized hours, stronger worker demand for hours, or both, but do not identify the underlying mechanism.
title: Education and the Decline in Average Hours Worked

abstract: External borrowing by governments is widely viewed as an important instrument for financing development, yet its growth effects remain controversial. We exploit the bilateral structure of public sector lending relationships to construct plausibly exogenous foreign credit supply shocks, isolating changes in borrowing capacity arising from creditorspecific shifts in lending rather than borrower demand. Using data covering 134 developing economies over 1970-2023, we show that positive foreign credit supply shocks lead to persistent increases in public investment and external indebtedness. However, easier access to external public sector finance does not, on average, generate sustained improvements in output or productivity and is accompanied by real exchange rate appreciation, weaker external balances, and partial crowding-out of private investment. The macroeconomic benefits of external public sector borrowing depend critically on institutional quality. Countries with stronger institutions translate additional borrowing into more favorable productivity and output responses, while accumulating more public capital and relying less on domestic financing. Our findings suggest that greater access to external finance is not, by itself, sufficient to boost development. The effectiveness of public sector borrowing depends fundamentally on the institutional capacity to allocate and manage borrowed resources productively.
authors: Marijn A. Bolhuis & Tobias Krahnke & Mr. Papa M N
title: Does Foreign Borrowing Lift Growth?

abstract: Despite the increasing use of asset purchase programs (APPs) by central banks over the past two decades, the economic literature has not empirically investigated how APPs are conducted from a cross-country perspective. Furthermore, a complete picture and critical details of APPs around the world remains lacking, particularly for small advanced economies and emerging markets. This paper fills this information gap by constructing a comprehensive global database on central bank asset purchase programs for the entire universe of advanced economies and emerging markets with monetary autonomy from 2008 to 2024. Our findings show that most central banks have conducted APPs, which have displayed heterogeneous characteristics, witnessed greater usage, and covered major asset classes beyond conventional government debt securities. The empirical analysis suggests that while triggers of APPs during 2008-2009 seem to be idiosyncratic across economies, disinflationary risks and government bond market volatilities activated the use of APPs in 2020. Furthermore, central banks that are constrained by the Zero Lower Bound and operate in countries with high public debt to GDP ratios tend to have longer buying durations of APPs. Finally, the pace of APPs depends on their previous pace as well as real GDP growth and CPI inflation and differs between buying and unwinding phases.
title: How Do Monetary Authorities Buy Publicly Traded Financial Assets? A Cross-Country Database and an Empirical Study of Central Bank Asset Purchase Programs

abstract: This paper investigates how shocks to the U.S. long-term risk-neutral interest rate influence emerging market local currency sovereign bonds and how domestic investor participation affects this relationship. We focus on the expected-future-short-rate, or risk-neutral, component of U.S. long-term rates, which reflects U.S. monetary policy and serves as a purer from of the global risk-free benchmark, rather than term premia. Using the instrumental variable approach and data on investor types in local currency sovereign bond markets, we have two main findings. First, a rise in the U.S. long-term interest rate leads to an increase in both local currency sovereign yields and term premia in emerging markets. Second, domestic investor participation mitigates these spillover effects from the U.S. interest rate, primarily driven by domestic banks and non-bank institutional investors rather than central banks. These results underscore the importance of policies aimed at broadening and deepening local investor bases to strengthen local market resilience against unexpected external interest-rate shocks.
title: Transmission of U.S. Long-term Rate to EM Local Currency Sovereign Bonds: The Role of the Investor Composition

abstract: This paper presents a methodology for downscaling official national and subnational macroeconomic data into high-resolution grids using spatial machine learning techniques. Traditional macroeconomic data are highly aggregated and obscure the spatial distributions needed to understand and quantify local economic activity, impacts of physical risks, and infrastructure gaps. Our hierarchical approach integrates official macroeconomic accounts with Earth observation predictors, such as nighttime lights, built-up areas, land cover, and gridded population, to deliver high-resolution, gridded estimates that remain fully consistent with official subnational and national totals. The empirical application focuses on constructing experimental gridded GDP by ten-sector industry for Canada and the United States. The methodology complements and enhances official statistics by adding spatial granularity through open geospatial datasets and can be extended to generate gridded capital stock estimates.
authors: Mr. Marco Marini & Jim Tebrake & Andinet Woldemichael
title: Earth Observations and Machine Learning for Gridded Macroeconomic Data

abstract: Central counterparties (CCPs) have become pivotal to financial stability in the post-Global-Financial-Crisis era by mitigating contagion in interconnected markets through the management of counterparty credit risk—the risk that the opposing party in a financial transaction fails to deliver payments or assets. Traditional risk assessments of CCPs primarily address the impact of member or client defaults on CCP liquidity and solvency. This paper introduces a framework that expands this focus to include investment risks associated with the significant cash CCPs hold as margin and applies it to CCPs operating in – or of systematic importance for – the European Union (EU). Specifically, we analyze ‘non-default’ losses stemming from market risk and counterparty credit risk within CCPs’ cash investment strategies. Our findings show that the impact of market risk is generally contained due to strict eligibility criteria and the short duration of investments. However, counterparty credit risk from reverse repo exposures can be substantial, with frequently insufficient haircuts that do not provide sufficient protection against collateral devaluation, posing the potential to significantly deplete available CCP resources. Quantifying these risks sheds light on how margin calls can transmit financial stress from capital markets into money markets via CCPs’ cash management practices.
authors: Elisa Letizia & Pierpaolo Grippa & Franck Viollet
title: Beyond Clearing: Central Counterparties’ Investment and Risk Management of Cash from Margin Calls

abstract: This paper constructs a country-level panel of estimated international stablecoin flows, covering 188 countries, totaling $21.4 trillion in gross flows between 2018 and 2025. Activity is disproportionately concentrated in emerging markets and developing economies, which hold three quarters of stablecoins. When countries restrict capital outflows, stablecoin activity rises by roughly 30 percent over the following six months, then plateaus, and does not fall back when restrictions are removed. When currency crises hit, stablecoin holdings increase by roughly 75 percent within a year, and the new holdings persist. Both findings suggest that dollarization may now also operate through stablecoins.
title: International Stablecoin Flows, Capital Controls and Currency Crises

abstract: Young workers adopt new technologies at higher rates than old workers. I develop an overlappinggenerations model linking this lifecycle gradient to technology adoption, wages, and innovation. Using U.S. commuting-zone variation and a historical-births instrument, I show that younger workforces expand computerscience employment and raise wages, especially for young workers. Exposure through trade to youth waves in foreign markets also increases R&D employment and patenting. Calibrated to these responses, the model attributes about one quarter of the late-1990s U.S. productivity acceleration to the baby boom’s youth wave, partly recasting the IT boom as a demographic episode. Aging workforces therefore create a headwind to endogenous technology adoption and innovation.
title: The Demographics of Technology Adoption and Productivity Growth

abstract: This paper presents a stress test framework for nonfinancial corporate (NFC) balance sheets. The model simulates firm income statements and balance sheets conditional on macro-financial scenarios, to obtain conventional risk metrics such as probabilities of default (PDs) and loss given default (LGD), alongside other structural metrics such as interest coverage ratios, leverage, and others. The model entails explicit stock–flow accounting and a link of borrowing costs to firm-specific credit risk metrics, i.e., an endogenous cost of funding feedback. An illustration is provided with an application to Brazil, involving 8,000 private firms and three hundred listed nonfinancial firms. The results point to heightened vulnerabilities under stagflation shock scenarios, which jointly weaken earnings and raise funding costs, increasing default risk and debt at risk.
title: Corporate Sector Stress Testing with Endogenous Balance Sheet Dynamics

abstract: We study whether buyer-supplier relationships feature complementarities in intangible inputs. Using administrative data from the Dominican Republic, we show that foreign demand routed through intangible-intensive buyers raises a supplier’s own intangible purchase share, while demand from other buyers has no effect. Two event studies on firms not previously exposed to intangible-producing partners provide further evidence. Forming a first link with an intangible-industry buyer raises the probability of any intangible purchase by about 4 percentage points, and hiring a worker from an intangible-producing firm for the first time has an effect of the same size. A general equilibrium production network model with endogenous intangible input use, knowledge transfer through worker mobility, and endogenous intangible prices implies that supply-chain complementarities account for about 15 percent of aggregate intangible purchases and about 4 percent of output.
authors: Marvin Cardoza & Mr. Francesco Grigoli & Mr. Nicola Pierri

title: Intangible Input Complementarities Along Supply Chains

abstract: This paper evaluates the effects of the European Union’s (EU) regional trade agreements (RTAs) on trade patterns, with a particular focus on diversification. Using a structural gravity model with data for 170 industries, we exploit variation in RTA depth, measured by the number of legally enforceable provisions, to estimate the effects of deep trade agreements, allowing for heterogeneity across sectors. We then use these estimates to evaluate recent and prospective EU agreements, including EU–Mercosur and EU–India, by analyzing their legal texts and constructing novel measures of agreement depth. The results show that deeper RTAs significantly increase bilateral trade, with substantial sectoral heterogeneity, and promote diversification across products and trading partners. Counterfactual general equilibrium simulations indicate that new agreements further strengthen diversification by reducing import concentration, including in green and strategic sectors, thereby enhancing supply chain resilience.
authors: Francesca Caselli & Alen Mulabdic & Michele Ruta

title: EU Trade Diversification Through Regional Trade Agreements

abstract: This paper examines the determinants of policy responses to the 2026 energy shock using the newly constructed IMF Global Policy Tracker. The main analysis focuses on measures announced between end-February and early June, while preliminary data through mid-September shed light on how policy responses evolved as energy prices began to normalize. The findings point to distinct drivers of policy composition and design. At average public debt levels, greater shock exposure is associated with a larger share of price pass-through measures. As debt rises, this association strengthens, while the relationship between exposure and fiscal shielding weakens. Monetary responses are driven mainly by pre-shock inflation developments, while financial-stabilization measures are more closely associated with reserve adequacy. Policy design—including targeting and temporariness—is shaped more by institutional capacity, inflation, and the political cycle than by shock exposure. The extended dataset shows a gradual shift away from fiscal shielding toward pass-through, demand- and inflation- management measures. Later announcements are more likely to identify beneficiaries but less likely to include explicit expiry dates or sunset provisions. The main findings broadly hold, although some become less statistically significant.
authors: Tohid Atashbar & Yidan Cheng & Leonardo Indraccolo & Jackson Mandel & Tiffany Munoz-Zegarra & Mr. Atsushi Oshima & Noor Rahman & Mr. Sergio L. Rodriguez & Sahra Sakha & Christoph Ungerer & Ms. Aleksandra Zdzienicka
title: What Drives Policy Responses to the 2026 Energy Shock? First Evidence from the IMF Global Policy Tracker

abstract: There is substantial heterogeneity in economic, educational, and health outcomes among American Indians, shaped by factors such as geographic location, resource endowments, and historical experiences with federal policies. There is clear evidence that past policies, including forced relocation, boarding schools, and assimilation efforts, have had long-lasting negative effects on human capital development and intergenerational mobility. Recent decades have seen improvements in some areas, particularly where tribes have exercised greater self-governance and implemented innovative economic development strategies. This paper emphasizes that a “one-size-fits-all” approach is inadequate for analyzing the sources and potential remediation of disparities between Native populations and descendants of later arrivals. Measures for American Indian outcomes are complicated by issues of racial and tribal identification, data limitations, and changing definitions. This article comments on the need for caution and clarity in the use and analysis of data for this population in both historical and contemporary settings.
title: Beyond the Conventional Narrative: Economic Heterogeneity and Human Capital among American Indians
